newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/January positions being closed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/January positions being closed.

text.p: January options expire at the end of the week and traders said investors had begun to close out positions on Monday.
"Mostly we're getting people closing out January positions," one broker said, adding that options on technology stocks again appeared to be the most active.
Among options on technology stocks, Intel Corp options were busy as the stock reached another all-time high.
By around 1130 CST/1730 GMT, Intel shares were ahead 1-7/8 at 146-3/8, just off their session high of 146-3/4. Volume was around six million shares.
The broker said some investors were rolling January Intel positions out and others were taking profits.
The January series was most active, led by the 150 call, which traded about 4,035 contracts. The option, which had open interest of 13,875 through last Friday, gained 9/16 to 2-3/8.
The Intel January 145 call traded 2,970 contracts, making it second most active in the group. The option rose one to 4-5/8. Its open interest was 14,490.
The only Intel put with more than 1,000 contracts changing hands was the February 125, with volume of about 1,090. That option lost 3/8 to 1-3/8. Its open interest was 2,322.
Intel is scheduled to report quarterly earnings Tuesday.
Traders said despite the coming flood of quarterly earnings releases, investors did not appear to be using options for earnings-related protection or speculation.
Earnings "haven't really been a factor for us too much," the broker said. "It's mostly expiration maintenance that we're seeing."
Other active technology stock options included another chip maker, Advanced Micro Devices Inc.
Advanced Micro shares rallied two to 29-3/4 after Morgan Stanley initiated coverage with an outperform rating.
On the Pacific Stock Exchange, the Advanced Micro January 30 call traded about 3,470 contracts, making it the most active option on that exchange.
Among other Advanced Micro options, the January 25 call traded about 1,020 contracts, the January 30 put about 620 and the January 27-1/2 put 560.
Also on the Pacific Stock Exchange, several options on Sun Microsystems Inc, led by the January 30 call, drew solid interest. The January 30 call traded 3,445 contracts.
The January 27-1/2 call, the January 25 put and the February 30 call also were active.
Perennially active International Business Machines Corp had a few options on the most actives list at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
The heaviest equity volume at the CBOE was in the Callaway Golf Co February 30 call, which traded about 4,270 contracts. Its open interest was 3,439.
A trader in the options said a trade of 4,130 of those contracts was a buy-write, also known as a covered write.
The trader said the investor already owned the stock and simply went short the call options to complete the buy-write. ((-G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
